Thanks Ben — and thanks Aisha for the quick reply.

Ben — I reviewed the mapping and found two root causes for the mismatch:
1) Tokenization aliasing: Fortis exported the staging token (FF24) into their billing template. We can either alias FF24 to FF23 in our procurement ledger (fast), or reissue a new PO token to Fortis and require them to resubmit invoices (cleaner audit trail).
2) Line-item misclassification: ~7 line codes from Fortis (including FC-SVC-004) map to our compute SKU but were billed to a consultancy code on their side. That will cause spend to hit an unintended budget bucket and could trigger an overrun on the consultancy spend cap.

Recommendation (minimizes customer disruption):
- Create an alias in Ledger: map PO-2026-FF24 -> PO-2026-FF23. This will ensure invoices clear against the intended PO and the spend cap enforces correctly.
- Meanwhile, ask Fortis to correct line_code for the disputed items on their next invoice batch (we can accept a corrected credit + rebill if needed).
- Put a temporary spend hold on the consultancy budget for Fortis (Finance to allow only essential items until we reconcile).

I’ve prepared a corrected PO worksheet (attached) with suggested remaps and the list of affected invoice ids. Please confirm if Finance is okay with an alias versus reissue. If Finance prefers reissue, we’ll need to abort aliasing and issue new PO token PO-20261101-RW-77 and instruct Fortis to use that going forward.

Action items:
- Kimberly: can you confirm temporary spend hold and whether aliasing is acceptable?
- Ben: please ping the customer success lead and integration engineer to ensure they won’t fail the API on token mismatch during go-live.
